messages:
nina: quick question: if we standardize proto-first internal APIs, how do we handle client codegen for dynamic languages? can't expect teams to run protoc during deploy.
omar: publish prebuilt clients to internal npm/pip registries tied to service proto version. publish semver packages.
claire: registry approach works but slow for fast iteration. alternative: provide a light runtime adapter that introspects proto descriptors via HTTP and does dynamic marshalling in-process.
nina: dynamic marshalling is convenient but loses type checks and CI linting. prefer generated clients for critical infra.
omar: maybe split: generated clients for platform infra & high-volume services; dynamic adapters for small product teams.
sre-bot: FYI: existing monitoring dashboards assume JSON payload sizes; proto-packed messages will change token accounting.
claire: that's why we need size-metrics at gateway and rpc layer. Console should normalize token accounting across formats.
nina: also think about backwards compatibility: a service adds a new repeated field. older generated clients might ignore it; dynamic adapters can surface unknowns. need clear deprecation policy.
omar: propose proto change policy: minor changes allowed; major (breaking) require migration plan and Console warning with scheduled enforcement date.
claire: action items: 1) client registry guide (omar) 2) dynamic adapter prototype (claire) 3) console deprecation warning UI (nina) 4) metric normalization for proto vs json (sre-bot)
omar: will start registry doc. gotovo.
